title: A Tour of Antique Plumbing and the Toilet of the Future (Ask This Old House)

locations.name: Boston, MA (historical context for origins of the family business)
locations.basis: Transcript notes founders were Boston firefighters and mentions a local Boston foundry; these are historical context rather than filming location.

summary: This This Old House segment pairs a historical tour of plumbing fixtures with a look at a modern, high-tech toilet. It traces the evolution from the earliest, nonstandard lead piping to the rise of standardized, mass-produced baths in the early 20th century, illustrated with artifacts, engravings, and a 1930 catalog that introduces the Neo-angle bath. It also discusses retrofit challenges in older housing (even fitting a bathroom into unlikely spaces). The episode culminates in a contemporary demonstration of a “toilet of the future” featuring a sensor-activated, no-touch interface, a heated seat, a built-in bidet with UV self-cleaning, odor control, a nightlight, and automatic lid and flush capabilities—blending historical context with a current technology showcase.
topics: Bathroom retrofits/integrating baths in tight spaces

sections.title: Origins and nonstandard beginnings of plumbing
sections.description: Introduces the earliest days of plumbing with lead piping and nonstandard fittings, highlighting the ad hoc nature of early installations and artifacts from local foundries; frames plumbing history as a family business with deep roots in Boston.

sections.title: From custom to standardized fixtures (early 20th century)
concepts: Neo-angle bath (advertised as bath of the future)
sections.description: Discusses the move from handmade, custom fixtures to standardized, nationally manufactured baths. Includes references to a 1930 catalog, the Neo-angle bath concept, and the shift to a standardized 4 ft x 4 ft bathing well and related bath/shower configurations.

sections.title: Retrofit and placement of bathrooms in old houses
sections.description: Covers how 20th-century housing stock was retrofitted with bathrooms, including plans to fit a bath into unlikely spaces like stairwells or front halls, illustrating evolving urban housing needs.

sections.title: The Toilet of the Future: features and demonstration
sections.description: Showcases a modern, sensor-activated toilet with a non-contact interface, a heated seat, a built-in bidet that activates with a skin-sensor cue, UV self-cleaning for the bidet, odor-control features, a nightlight, and an automatic lid/flush system, presented with humor and context about past bathroom innovations.

featured_techniques.technique: Built-in bidet with UV self-cleaning cycle
